adversarialFindings.title: The rulings do not cover three of the six sub-12px declarations in scope.
adversarialFindings.detail: G1 names exactly three: .cite em at 11px, .cite.model .corpus at 10px, .mxgroup .lic at 10px. The four-family port carries three MORE: .atomchip at 10px, .atomchip .did at 10px, .basisline at 11px. G6 pulled .basisline into scope without re-running G1 over it, and .atomchip is the ONE declaration 30b section 1.3 grants a named exception to: 'the evidence chip label may set at 10px'.
adversarialFindings.conflict: 30b section 1.3 says the evidence chip label MAY set at 10px. src/type-conformance.test.mjs makes the floor absolute, and its own comment states the reason: 'the one named 10px exception is the evidence chip, which does not exist in this product, so the floor is absolute here.' This PR is what makes that component exist, so the test's stated premise is falsified by the very change it is gating.
adversarialFindings.decision: Ship all six at 12px. Do NOT weaken the gate.
adversarialFindings.reasoning: Three sources say absolute and one says otherwise. (1) The dispatch hard-constraint list: 'No font declaration below 12px anywhere in shell.css after your change.' (2) WDLL item 2's graded check: 'zero font declarations below 12px in shell.css'. (3) G1's headline is that the type floor HOLDS, with the consequence already accepted in writing: '30b's own specimens stop matching what ships, and 30b is now the looser document.' Only 30b section 1.3's exception text points the other way, and G1 explicitly deprecates 30b as the looser document. Weakening a proven-able-to-fire gate to admit a spec exception is the DEV_PROCESS 2.2 anti-pattern; shipping at 12px keeps the gate intact and is a one-line reversal per declaration if the operator rules the other way.
adversarialFindings.flaggedTo: operator, loudly, in the close. This is the single call the rulings did not cover.

adversarialFindings.title: G2 resolves .atomchip.web to a semantically wrong cursor.
adversarialFindings.detail: 30b declares no cursor on .atomchip.web, so it inherits cursor:pointer from the base .atomchip rule. 30c declares cursor:default. 30c's own markup specimen at line 1955 is a span, non-interactive, and 30c section 6.3 says an unverified web source is not a recorded source and carries no atom, so it does not open. G2 says every divergence resolves to 30b, so the shipped .web chip advertises a pointer for something that cannot be clicked.
adversarialFindings.decision: Ship 30b. The ruling is not mine to revisit. Named as DIV-5 in the close with the value shipped and the consequence stated.
adversarialFindings.reasoning: G2 is unconditional: every divergence resolves to 30b. Executor discretion here would be exactly the silent-resolution failure the ruling exists to prevent.

adversarialFindings.title: The dispatch's 'every size and radius must be an existing var(--sc-*)' is stricter than the product and than the enforcing test.
adversarialFindings.detail: 30b's own rules carry literal geometry constants that map to NO shipping token: border-radius 3px on .mxgroup .lic, border-radius 1px and width 11px and height 4px on .meter i, the 3px rail column and 132px section column on .mxrow, min-height 42px, gap 1px on .cite.model. The only radius tokens that ship are --sc-r-control 4px, --sc-r 6px, --sc-r-lg 8px, --sc-r-full 999px.
adversarialFindings.evidence: web/shell.css already ships literal 'border-radius: 3px' at lines 19, 127, 451 and 544 on main. The enforcing test (type-conformance) checks hex, rgb() and --sc-* declarations only; it does not check literal lengths.
adversarialFindings.decision: Keep 30b's literal geometry constants verbatim. Snapping .lic's 3px radius to --sc-r-control at 4px would be an unruled design change, and the zero-new-tokens constraint is about not FORKING the kit, which literal geometry does not do.
adversarialFindings.reasoning: The constraint's teeth are the three the test enforces. Reading it as 'no literal length' would make the port impossible without inventing tokens, which the same constraint forbids.

adversarialFindings.title: Raising the size could clip if a line-height ends up below the new font size.
adversarialFindings.detail: Checked every one of the six raised declarations: .cite em has no line-height of its own and inherits 16px from .cite; .cite.model .corpus is 13px; .mxgroup .lic is unitless 1 which resolves to 12px; .atomchip is 14px; .atomchip .did is 14px; .basisline is 16px. None falls below 12px, so no line-height needs to move.
adversarialFindings.decision: Locked port principle: change ONLY the size number. Every line-height, weight, tracking, colour and geometry stays exactly as 30b drew it.
adversarialFindings.reasoning: It is the tightest auditable diff and it happens to preserve a real property: .atomchip at 12px/14px with 2px padding stays 20px tall, the same height as .pill and .prov, so the chip row rhythm is unchanged. Raising the line-height to 16px would have broken it.

adversarialFindings.title: Three meanings now share the token 'rail'.
adversarialFindings.detail: .srcreg .rail is a severity rail; .colstack.rail is a LAYOUT modifier meaning the 380px context-rail column; .mxrow > .rail and .finding > .rail add a third. Every rule is scoped so there is no CSS conflict, and the kit counts bare tokens so the denominator does not move.
adversarialFindings.decision: Accept and record. Renaming is not in this row's scope.

adversarialFindings.title: G3, whether .mxgroup carries a section count, needs no CSS.
adversarialFindings.detail: 30c's .mxgroup specimen adds a grow spacer with an inline flex:1 plus a .t-caption section count. The product already ships '.panel-head .grow, .grow { flex: 1; }' at web/shell.css:192, so the spacer works with no inline style and no new rule, and .t-caption ships at line 61.
adversarialFindings.decision: No rule added. This item is CSS-only and adds no markup, so G3 is a markup question that lands with the screens at WDLL item 9, not here.
